rows.title: All eyes on Lamont as CT’s hunger crisis worsens
rows.standfirst: Advocates are increasingly impatient with Gov. Ned Lamont’s response to a worsening hunger crisis in the wake of cuts to SNAP.

rows.title: Lamont orders $300 grocery gift cards for residents losing SNAP
rows.standfirst: CT will provide the benefit to an estimated 25,000 residents who’ve lost federal nutrition assistance. Cards will be distributed by August.

rows.title: Can CT make big debt payments while boosting towns, services?
rows.standfirst: If CT can’t find the right balance between paying down debt and supporting towns and public services, deficits are coming, analysts say.

rows.title: CT says its tax system is unfair, but changes would mean tradeoffs
rows.standfirst: While the call for tax reform gains momentum, major proposals cannot get past a governor who is focused paying down CT’s huge pension debt.

rows.title: About 110,000 poor CT adults could lose Medicaid coverage
rows.standfirst: CT officials are scrambling to avert a swell in uninsured patients forced to seek care through hospital emergency departments.

rows.title: Fazio offers plan to ease CT’s property tax burdens
rows.standfirst: Republican gubernatorial candidate Ryan Fazio offered a blueprint Wednesday to reduce CT’s over-reliance on the municipal property tax.

rows.title: CT poised to invest again in childcare, pay down pension debt
rows.standfirst: The state budget is on pace for $412M surplus, all earmarked for childcare. Separately, $1B in off-budget savings will shrink pension debt.
